# BELL'S PALSY

Herpes simplex and varicella-zoster are possible causes of Bell's palsy. Others include Borrelia burgdorferi trauma. Some cases are idiopathic. Risk factors for for Bell's Palsy include pregnancy, diabetes, obesity, hypertension, and upper respiratory infections. Neurology consult is encouraged.

If Lyme disease is suspected, refer to the Lyme disease treatment page:
[Lyme Disease](lyme-disease)

Treatment with prednisone and an antiviral within 72 hours of symptoms onset improves the chances of a complete recovery.

- Up-To-Date article: Bell's palsy: Treatment and prognosis in adults
Therapy:
Preferred:
Prednisone 60 mg q24h PO for 7 days <AND> valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h ($) [R] for 7 days

Alternative:
Prednisone 60 mg q24h PO for 7 days <AND> acyclovir 400 mg PO q6h ($) [R] for 10 days
